headline: Dow Surges Past 12,500 as Earnings Season Begins
summary: Markets open the second quarter strong as corporate earnings expectations remain upbeat. Consumer confidence is high and housing starts are still near record levels.

headline: New Century Financial Files for Bankruptcy
summary: New Century Financial, once the second-largest subprime mortgage lender in the U.S., files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy after lenders cut off its credit lines. The company had originated $60 billion in loans in 2006.

headline: Existing Home Sales Decline for Second Straight Month
summary: The National Association of Realtors reports existing home sales fell 8.4% from a year ago. Median home prices slip in several major markets for the first time in years.

headline: Dow Jones Hits Record High Above 13,000
summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average closes above 13,000 for the first time in history, driven by strong corporate profits and merger activity.

headline: Daimler Sells Chrysler to Cerberus Capital
summary: DaimlerChrysler sells 80% of its Chrysler unit to private equity firm Cerberus Capital for $7.4 billion, ending its troubled nine-year merger experiment.

headline: Bear Stearns Hedge Funds Report Heavy Subprime Losses
summary: Two Bear Stearns hedge funds heavily invested in subprime mortgage-backed securities report steep losses. The funds had been leveraged at more than 10-to-1.

headline: Merrill Lynch Seizes $800 Million From Bear Stearns Funds
summary: Merrill Lynch moves to seize and sell collateral from the troubled Bear Stearns hedge funds. Other Wall Street firms begin pulling back from subprime exposure.

headline: S&P and Moody's Slash Ratings on Billions in Subprime Bonds
summary: S&P places $12 billion in subprime mortgage bonds on credit watch for possible downgrade. Moody's downgrades $5 billion worth. The AAA ratings that justified these investments are crumbling.

headline: Dow Hits All-Time High of 14,000
summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average breaches 14,000 for the first time. Analysts celebrate but some warn the rally is built on shaky credit foundations.

headline: Bear Stearns Hedge Funds File for Bankruptcy
summary: Bear Stearns' two troubled hedge funds that invested in subprime mortgages file for bankruptcy, reporting nearly total losses for investors.

headline: American Home Mortgage Files for Bankruptcy
summary: American Home Mortgage Investment Corp., the tenth-largest retail mortgage lender in the U.S., files for Chapter 11 after failing to fund new loans.

headline: BNP Paribas Freezes Three Funds, Credit Markets Seize Up
summary: French bank BNP Paribas halts redemptions on three investment funds citing inability to value subprime assets. The European Central Bank injects 95 billion euros into the banking system overnight.

headline: Fed Cuts Discount Rate in Emergency Move
summary: The Federal Reserve cuts the discount rate by half a percentage point to 5.75% in an unscheduled move, acknowledging that credit conditions have deteriorated significantly.

headline: Northern Rock Suffers First British Bank Run in 150 Years
summary: Depositors queue around the block to withdraw savings from Northern Rock after the British bank seeks emergency funding from the Bank of England.

headline: Fed Slashes Federal Funds Rate by Half a Point
summary: The Federal Reserve cuts its benchmark rate by 50 basis points to 4.75%, a larger cut than expected. Markets surge on hopes the Fed will prevent a recession.

headline: UBS Reports $3.4 Billion Subprime Write-Down
summary: Swiss banking giant UBS announces a $3.4 billion write-down on subprime-related positions. More major bank losses are expected to follow.

headline: Dow Hits Record Close of 14,164
summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average reaches its all-time closing high. This will be the peak — the index will not return to this level for over five years.

headline: Major Banks Form $75 Billion Superfund to Calm Markets
summary: Citigroup, JPMorgan Chase, and Bank of America announce a plan to create a fund to buy distressed mortgage assets. Critics call it a band-aid.

headline: Merrill Lynch Reports $7.9 Billion in Write-Downs
summary: Merrill Lynch stuns Wall Street with $7.9 billion in subprime-related write-downs, nearly double initial estimates. CEO Stan O'Neal is ousted days later.

headline: Fed Cuts Rates Again to 4.5%
summary: The Federal Reserve cuts the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 4.50%, its second cut in six weeks. The housing downturn shows no signs of easing.

headline: Citigroup CEO Prince Resigns Over Mounting Losses
summary: Citigroup CEO Charles Prince resigns after the bank discloses up to $11 billion in subprime exposure. Citigroup is now the most troubled of the major banks.

headline: Abu Dhabi Invests $7.5 Billion in Citigroup
summary: The Abu Dhabi Investment Authority buys a $7.5 billion stake in Citigroup, providing desperately needed capital. The deal highlights how weakened U.S. banks have become.

headline: Bush Announces Subprime Mortgage Relief Plan
summary: President Bush unveils a plan to freeze interest rates on some adjustable-rate subprime mortgages for five years. Critics say it helps too few homeowners.

headline: Fed Cuts Rates to 4.25%, Markets Disappointed
summary: The Federal Reserve cuts the federal funds rate by 25 basis points, but markets tumble because investors had hoped for a larger half-point reduction.

headline: Morgan Stanley Reports $9.4 Billion Write-Down
summary: Morgan Stanley writes down $9.4 billion in mortgage-related losses and sells a $5 billion stake to China Investment Corporation to shore up its balance sheet.

headline: Countrywide Sold to Bank of America for $4 Billion
summary: Bank of America agrees to buy Countrywide Financial, the nation's largest mortgage lender, for $4 billion — a fraction of its peak value. The deal includes massive toxic mortgage exposure.

headline: Citigroup Posts $9.8 Billion Quarterly Loss
summary: Citigroup reports a $9.83 billion loss for the fourth quarter, its worst ever, driven by $18 billion in write-downs on subprime mortgage assets.

headline: Fed Makes Emergency Rate Cut of 75 Basis Points
summary: In its first emergency rate cut since 2001, the Federal Reserve slashes the federal funds rate by 75 basis points to 3.50% as global markets plunge.

headline: Fed Cuts Again to 3.0%, Two Cuts in Eight Days
summary: The Federal Reserve cuts rates by another 50 basis points, bringing the federal funds rate to 3.0%. Two rate cuts in eight days signals deep concern about the economy.

headline: Bush Signs $168 Billion Stimulus Package
summary: President Bush signs an economic stimulus package that will send tax rebate checks of up to $600 per individual to 130 million Americans.

headline: Britain Nationalizes Northern Rock
summary: The British government takes Northern Rock into public ownership after private bids fail. It is the first nationalization of a British bank since the 1970s.

headline: Bear Stearns Nears Collapse, Gets Emergency Fed Loan
summary: Bear Stearns receives emergency funding from the Federal Reserve through JPMorgan Chase after a run on the bank depletes its cash reserves in days.

headline: JPMorgan Buys Bear Stearns for $2 Per Share
summary: JPMorgan Chase agrees to buy Bear Stearns for just $2 per share with Fed backing — the stock had traded at $170 a year earlier. The price is later raised to $10.

headline: Fed Cuts Rates to 2.25%, Opens Lending to Investment Banks
summary: The Federal Reserve cuts rates by 75 basis points and opens its discount window to investment banks for the first time since the Great Depression.

headline: Deutsche Bank Reports $3.9 Billion in Write-Downs
summary: Deutsche Bank becomes the latest global bank to report massive subprime-related losses. Banks worldwide have now written down more than $200 billion.

headline: Fed Cuts Rates to 2.0%
summary: The Federal Reserve reduces the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 2.0%, its seventh cut since September 2007. The rate has been halved in seven months.

headline: Oil Prices Surge Past $130 Per Barrel
summary: Crude oil breaks $130 for the first time amid growing demand from China and supply concerns. Gasoline prices hit record highs across the United States.

headline: Moody's and S&P Warn of Possible Downgrade for Major Bond Insurers
summary: Rating agencies threaten to downgrade MBIA and Ambac, the two largest bond insurers. A downgrade would trigger forced selling of hundreds of billions in bonds they guarantee.

headline: Two Bear Stearns Hedge Fund Managers Arrested
summary: FBI arrests two former Bear Stearns hedge fund managers on charges of securities fraud and conspiracy for allegedly lying to investors about the funds' subprime exposure.

headline: Oil Hits All-Time High of $147 Per Barrel
summary: Crude oil prices reach a record $147.27 per barrel. Airline stocks plunge as fuel costs threaten to bankrupt several carriers.

headline: IndyMac Bank Seized by Federal Regulators
summary: The FDIC seizes IndyMac Bancorp, making it one of the largest bank failures in U.S. history. Depositors line up to withdraw funds, reminiscent of Depression-era bank runs.

headline: Treasury and Fed Announce Rescue Plan for Fannie and Freddie
summary: Treasury Secretary Paulson and Fed Chairman Bernanke announce emergency support for Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, which own or guarantee $5 trillion in mortgages.

headline: Bush Signs Housing and Economic Recovery Act
summary: President Bush signs legislation creating a new regulator for Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac with authority to place them in conservatorship if needed.

headline: Oil Falls Below $115 as Global Demand Slows
summary: Crude oil drops sharply from its July peak as the economic slowdown spreads worldwide. Gas prices begin to ease from record highs.

headline: Government Seizes Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac
summary: The U.S. government places Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac into conservatorship, effectively nationalizing the two mortgage giants and backstopping $5 trillion in home loans.

headline: Lehman Brothers Reports $3.9 Billion Quarterly Loss
summary: Lehman Brothers reports a massive loss and announces plans to sell assets and spin off commercial real estate holdings. The stock plunges as investors lose confidence.

headline: Bank of America Agrees to Buy Merrill Lynch for $50 Billion
summary: Bank of America agrees to acquire Merrill Lynch in an emergency weekend deal as Wall Street scrambles to avoid a total collapse of the financial system.

headline: Lehman Brothers Files for Bankruptcy
summary: Lehman Brothers files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, the largest bankruptcy in U.S. history. The 158-year-old firm's collapse sends shockwaves through global financial markets.

headline: Fed Bails Out AIG With $85 Billion Emergency Loan
summary: The Federal Reserve provides an $85 billion emergency credit line to insurance giant AIG, which faces collapse due to its massive exposure to credit default swaps.

headline: Money Market Fund 'Breaks the Buck,' Investors Panic
summary: The Reserve Primary Fund falls below $1 per share due to Lehman losses, triggering a run on money market funds nationwide. The Treasury guarantees all money market fund assets.

headline: Paulson Proposes $700 Billion Bank Bailout Plan
summary: Treasury Secretary Hank Paulson proposes the Troubled Asset Relief Program (TARP) to buy toxic mortgage assets from banks. Markets rally sharply on the announcement.

headline: Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley Become Bank Holding Companies
summary: Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley convert to bank holding companies, ending the era of independent Wall Street investment banks and gaining access to Fed emergency lending.

headline: Washington Mutual Seized in Largest Bank Failure in U.S. History
summary: Federal regulators seize Washington Mutual and sell its banking operations to JPMorgan Chase for $1.9 billion. WaMu had $307 billion in assets.

headline: House Votes Down TARP Bailout, Dow Plunges 778 Points
summary: The House of Representatives rejects the $700 billion bailout bill 228-205. The Dow drops 778 points, its largest single-day point decline in history.

headline: Congress Passes Revised TARP Bailout Bill
summary: After adding tax breaks and raising FDIC insurance to $250,000, Congress passes the $700 billion TARP bailout. President Bush signs it immediately.

headline: Global Markets in Freefall, Dow Falls Below 10,000
summary: The Dow drops below 10,000 for the first time in four years as the credit crisis goes global. Iceland's banking system collapses entirely.

headline: Fed and Five Central Banks Coordinate Emergency Rate Cuts
summary: The Federal Reserve, ECB, Bank of England, and others simultaneously cut interest rates in unprecedented coordinated action to stem the financial panic.

headline: Treasury Injects $250 Billion Directly Into Banks
summary: Treasury Secretary Paulson shifts TARP strategy from buying toxic assets to injecting capital directly into nine major banks, including $25 billion each to JPMorgan, Citigroup, and Bank of America.

headline: Greenspan Admits 'Flaw' in Free-Market Ideology
summary: Former Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan tells Congress he found a flaw in the ideology that free markets could regulate themselves, calling it a 'once-in-a-century credit tsunami.'

headline: Barack Obama Elected 44th President
summary: Barack Obama is elected as the 44th President of the United States, defeating John McCain. Markets have already priced in the result but face deep uncertainty ahead.

headline: AIG Bailout Restructured and Expanded to $150 Billion
summary: The government restructures AIG's rescue package to $150 billion, nearly doubling the original bailout. AIG's credit default swap exposure was far larger than initially known.

headline: Big Three Automakers Plead for Congressional Bailout
summary: CEOs of GM, Ford, and Chrysler testify before Congress requesting $25 billion in emergency loans. They are criticized for flying to Washington on private jets.

headline: Government Agrees to $306 Billion Citigroup Rescue
summary: The U.S. government agrees to backstop $306 billion in Citigroup's troubled assets and inject another $20 billion in TARP funds. The bank's stock had fallen 60% in a week.

headline: NBER Declares Recession Began in December 2007
summary: The National Bureau of Economic Research officially declares the U.S. has been in recession since December 2007, confirming what markets have known for months.

headline: Madoff Arrested in $50 Billion Ponzi Scheme
summary: Former NASDAQ chairman Bernard Madoff is arrested for running the largest Ponzi scheme in history. Investors including banks, hedge funds, and charities lost an estimated $50 billion.

headline: Fed Cuts Rates to Near Zero
summary: The Federal Reserve reduces the federal funds rate to a range of 0-0.25%, effectively zero. With rates at the floor, the Fed announces it will use 'all available tools' including buying mortgage-backed securities.

headline: Bush Authorizes $17.4 Billion Auto Industry Bailout
summary: President Bush provides $17.4 billion in emergency TARP loans to GM and Chrysler after Congress fails to pass an auto bailout bill.

headline: December Jobs Report: 524,000 Lost, Unemployment at 7.2%
summary: The U.S. economy shed 524,000 jobs in December, bringing total 2008 job losses to 2.6 million — the most since 1945.

headline: Barack Obama Inaugurated as 44th President
summary: Barack Obama is sworn in as President, inheriting the worst financial crisis since the Great Depression. He pledges bold action to rescue the economy.

headline: Geithner Unveils Bank Rescue Plan, Markets Plunge
summary: Treasury Secretary Tim Geithner outlines a new financial stability plan but provides few details. The Dow drops nearly 400 points as investors are underwhelmed.

headline: Obama Signs $787 Billion Stimulus Into Law
summary: President Obama signs the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act, the largest economic stimulus package in U.S. history, combining tax cuts, infrastructure spending, and aid to states.

headline: AIG Posts $61.7 Billion Loss, Gets Fourth Bailout
summary: AIG reports a record $61.7 billion quarterly loss and receives its fourth government rescue. Total taxpayer commitment to AIG now exceeds $180 billion.

headline: Dow Closes Below 6,600, Down 54% From Peak
summary: The Dow Jones falls to 6,594, its lowest level since April 1997. The index has lost more than half its value from the October 2007 record high of 14,164.

headline: February Jobs Report: 651,000 Lost, Unemployment Hits 8.1%
summary: The economy sheds 651,000 jobs in February. Since the recession began in December 2007, the U.S. has lost 4.4 million jobs.

headline: Markets Hit Bottom: S&P 500 Closes at 676
summary: The S&P 500 closes at 676.53 and the Dow at 6,547.05, marking the lowest point of the financial crisis. From here, one of the greatest bull markets in history will begin.

headline: Fed Announces $1.2 Trillion in Quantitative Easing
summary: The Federal Reserve announces it will buy $300 billion in Treasury bonds and expand purchases of mortgage-backed securities to $1.25 trillion, launching large-scale quantitative easing.

headline: Geithner Unveils Public-Private Plan for Toxic Assets
summary: Treasury Secretary Geithner details a plan using public and private money to buy up to $1 trillion in toxic bank assets. Markets rally sharply on the specifics.
